messages.author: f69daf7445b84367
messages.subject: irregular variogram - periodogram interpretation
parts:
Dear Chris,
I am new to the use of R and am using CTMM package for dog home range analysis. The dogs used GPS tracking systems for about 20 days,  recording the location every 10 minutes and only when motion was detected. Therefore, if the dogs were resting for a long time, positions were not registered, likewise dogs inside the houses had obvious errors in the positions, so those data were eliminated (<2%).
I would like to ask you two questions:

1. The results in the attached variogram indicate that the individual is a resident? can I proceed with the rest of the analysis without problems?

2. I used the periograms (due to lack of night/rest data), following Appendix 2 S2, to test periodic behavior. I see a clear daily periodicity, but when I examine the diagnosis test, the patterns differ or do not overlap. Could this be to enough data availability? Would you suggest a different interpretation of these results? 

What would suggest me to do after following the steps of the CTMM package?


Thanks for your time,regards

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: irregular variogram - periodogram interpretation
parts:
Hi Lorena,

1.) That variogram looks very resident, so yes. After the initial increase, you can imagine a flat line going through all of that noise.
2.) I'm not exactly sure what your question is, but vignette('periodogram') covers periodic model selection. Periodograms are not going to be super insightful when there is periodicity in the collection of the data, which is what the diagnostic is for, and yours have peaks.

What steps to take after vignette('variogram') and vignette('akde'), etc.? I think that depends on what your research questions are. There is other functionality in the ctmm package, like speed() and overlap(). You can do post-hoc analysis on the results. There are also important movement analyses that are not in the ctmm package, like RSFs and SSFs.

Best,
Chris

That sounds like a bug I have fixed in the GitHub version of the package (not yet on CRAN), which you can install via

devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm")

If that doesn't fix the problem, then if you could please message/email me a copy of the problematic dataset, then I can take a look.

Best,
Chris
